goal: locate the growth that put a 31 minute mission at 30.07 GiB on a 31 GiB host and faulted it

symptom.rate: roughly 10 to 16 MiB per second of mission, tracking seconds rather than archived blocks
symptom.consequence: the 0.5 m/s full-area mission hit host memory pressure and faulted CAMERA_STATE_TIMEOUT with a camera service call outstanding

attribution.method: per-process RSS sampled every two seconds through a 3 x 2 m mission, once with the OptiX capture sensor and once without it

with_capture.window: 24 s to 84 s, after the scene load and before shutdown

other_processes.mission_operator: 44 to 98 MiB then flat, plus 41 MiB at the audit
other_processes.note: none of these grows at a rate that matters next to gz sim

attribution.verdict: the growth is in the gz sim process and it belongs to the capture path. With the linescan sensor off the same mission leaves that process essentially flat, a factor of twenty apart.

ruled_out: the sensor pose history, which is trimmed to eight samples per push
the C++ archive writer queue, bounded to two blocks in flight
the material tile cache, fixed at 32 slots on the device
RViz and the ROS bridge, both flat
not_yet_known: what inside the capture path accumulates. The rate does not scale with pixel production -- the rated mission produces six times the lines per second of the 0.5 m/s one and grows more slowly, not faster -- so retained image buffers are not a sufficient explanation on their own.
next: sample the gz sim heap by allocation site rather than by process
the per-exposure structures are the first place to look, since they are produced per line rather than per block

second_cut_stationary.method: one launch, vehicle never commanded to move, in two phases: plugin loaded with capture off, then capture enabled. A stationary vehicle never advances the encoder, so no line is ever triggered.

loaded_idle.window: after the scene finished loading at 36 s

second_cut_stationary.reading: merely having the plugin loaded costs about 2.3 MiB per second with the vehicle stopped, and enabling capture with no lines produced adds nothing measurable. The 9.7 MiB/s of a real mission is therefore about 2.3 of always-on growth plus about 7.4 that needs driving and line production.
second_cut_stationary.correction: the earlier comparison was "plugin loaded and capturing" against "plugin not loaded at all", which could not separate these.

third_cut_which_mapping.method: sample /proc/<gz sim>/maps and smaps_rollup every five seconds through a 3 x 2 m capture mission, grouped by mapping kind
third_cut_which_mapping.reading: the malloc heap and the small anonymous mappings are flat. All of the growth is resident pages in large anonymous mappings: about twenty new mappings of roughly 20 MiB each over 85 seconds, one every 4.3 s. A block of pixels is 16.0 MiB, so the size is the right order for an image buffer, but the mission archived only six blocks in that window, so it is not one per archived block.
what_this_rules_out: small-object accumulation in C++ containers, which would grow the brk heap
the tile cache and the pose history, both already bounded and both on other budgets
next: find the allocation of roughly 16 to 20 MiB in the capture path that is made about every four seconds and not reused
the ROS image publish path is the first suspect by size, and the per-exposure render batches by cadence

status: localised to large anonymous allocations in the capture path; the allocation site is not yet named
